title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exception Workflows
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational workflows for: RBAC and authentication; audit logging and log integrity; data residency and retention; secure software development lifecycle (SDLC); incident response for security events; compliance evidence collection and audit workflows; and risk & exception management. It is intended for engineering, security, product, and legal stakeholders.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-managed environments (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane) and associated management tooling and cloud accounts.
- Excludes customer-managed private deployments where the customer controls their own access settings; guidance still applies for our deployment tooling and onboarding checklists.

Ownership and contacts:
- Document owner: Security (security@redwood.example.com) - primary: Priya Malhotra
- Operational owners: Eng SRE (sre-oncall@redwood.example.com), Eng Infra (infra-oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Compliance/Legal contact: Legal (privacy-compliance@redwood.example.com)

1) RBAC & Authentication

Principles:
- Least privilege by default: roles grant the minimum permissions required to perform a job.
- Role-based grouping: personnel access is granted via team-based roles mapped to IdP groups (Okta).
- Separation of duties: production deployment and cost/finance actions are separated where practical.
- Short-lived tokens for automation: prefer short-lived STS credentials, OIDC where supported.

Role definitions (examples):
- security-admin: full security tooling and audit access (restricted).
- infra-ops: provisioning and network config in cloud accounts (no direct access to customer data buckets).
- svc-deploy: service accounts for CI/CD with deploy-only rights to specific namespaces/clusters.
- read-only-audit: access to logs and observability dashboards, no write privileges.

IdP & authentication configuration:
- Primary IdP: Okta SSO with SCIM group sync to cloud IAM.
- Enforce MFA (TOTP + hardware keys recommended) for all human users.
- Password policy enforced at IdP level: minimum length 14, banned-passwords list, 90-day rotation discouraged for MFA users.
- Service accounts: no shared human credentials. Use short-lived keys via Vault (HashiCorp Vault) or cloud-native STS.

Example AWS IAM policy snippet for read-only-audit role (JSON):
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "logs:GetLogEvents",
        "logs:DescribeLogGroups",
        "logs:DescribeLogStreams",
        "s3:GetObject",
        "s3:ListBucket"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:logs:us-*-*:log-group:/redwood/*",
        "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-log-archive/*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Access lifecycle & reviews:
- Quarterly access review for all high-privilege roles (security-admin, infra-ops, svc-deploy). Owners must attest in the Access Review board.
- Offboarding checklist: rapid IdP deprovisioning, revoke Vault tokens, rotate affected service credentials.

2) Audit Logging & Log Integrity

What we log:
- Authentication and authorization events (IdP: login, MFA failures, Okta admin actions).
- Privileged actions: role grants, policy changes, secret rotations.
- Data access: S3 object reads/writes on customer-data buckets, DB access events (where available).
- System events: deployments, autoscaler changes, infrastructure changes via IaC.
- Security detections: IDS/IPS alerts, WAF events, egress anomalies.

Logging pipeline and storage:
- Agents: Vector/Fluentd -> centralized Kafka/log buffer -> primary archive in encrypted S3 buckets (log-archive-{region}).
- Immutable retention: logs written to an append-only S3 prefix with object lock enabled for compliance-sensitive datasets.
- Indexing: security logs forwarded to Splunk/Datadog (depending on tenant) for search and alerting.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Log delivery: 99.9% of critical audit events delivered to archive within 5 minutes.
- Alerting: suspicious auth activity triggers high-priority pager within 1 minute.

Retention policy (default):
- Auth & admin logs: 7 years (business + compliance requirements).
- System & infra logs: 1 year (unless flagged for longer retention by product/customer contract).
- Sensitive customer access logs: align to contract (can be region-specific).

Log protection & integrity:
- Enable server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) for log archives.
- Enable S3 Object Lock (governance mode) for compliance buckets where required.
- Maintain automated checksum/hashing process and periodic integrity verification reports (monthly).

3) Data Residency & Retention

Residency principles:
- Customer data is stored only in regions contracted by the customer. Default hosted API region is us-west-2; customers can require eu-west-1 or other regions per contract.
- Backups and archives inherit primary data region unless explicit customer approval for cross-region replication is obtained.

Retention matrix (summary):
- Customer PII: configurable, default 7 years or per contract.
- Customer content (non-PII): default 1 year, configurable.
- Audit logs: see Audit Logging section.
- Backups: 90 days for rolling backups; long-term snapshots kept per customer SLA.

Sample retention table (ASCII):
| Data type | Default retention | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Customer PII | 7 years | product-privacy | Subject to legal holds |
| Chat logs (customer) | 1 year | product | Customers can request longer retention |
| Infra logs | 1 year | eng-sre | Can be extended for incident investigations |

Data deletion & legal holds:
- Deletion requests are executed via the Data Subject Request (DSR) workflow; DSRs must be routed to privacy-compliance@redwood.example.com.
- Legal holds override retention and must be coordinated with Legal.

4) Secure SDLC

Gates & tooling:
- Source control: GitHub with branch protection, required code owners, PR reviews (2 reviewers for production-impacting changes).
- CI: security scanning gates integrated in CI pipeline (Snyk/Trivy for SCA/container scanning, Semgrep for SAST rules).
- Secrets: no secrets in repos; detect with git-secrets and automated scanners.
- Dependency management: Dependabot or Renovate + weekly vulnerability triage.
- SBOM: generate SBOM for each release artifact.

Release policy:
- Canary rollouts for runtime changes; monitoring and automated rollback on error rate increase > 2x baseline or latency SLO violation.
- Security sign-off required for releases that touch auth, crypto, key management, or data access layers.

Developer training & awareness:
- Annual secure-coding training mandatory for engineering.
- Onboarding checklist includes account hygiene, MFA setup, and secure-SDLC basics.

5) Incident Response - Security Procedures

Classification and priorities:
- Sev-S (Security Severe): active data exfiltration, confirmed compromise of production secrets, or material customer data exposure.
- Sev-1: high-impact outages or broad service compromises.
- Sev-2/3: lower impact security events.

Typical incident lifecycle (high-level):
1. Detection & Triage: automated alerts or human detection -> Security Triage channel.
2. Containment: short-term containment steps (rotate keys, isolate hosts, apply WAF rules).
3. Eradication & Recovery: remove persistent artifacts, restore from clean backups, bring services back.
4. Post-incident review: timeline, root cause, remediation plan, lessons learned.

Roles & RACI highlights:
- Incident Commander (IC) - Security lead on-call (executes IR runbook).
- Communications owner - Customer success & comms for public/customer notifications.
- Tech lead - engineering owner responsible for technical remediation.
- Legal/Privacy - advise on disclosure, breach notification obligations.

Evidence preservation steps (immediate):
- Snapshot relevant logs, preserve disk images if required, capture process lists, network flows.
- Disable automatic log rotation for affected streams to avoid overwriting.
- Record chain of custody for all artifacts.

Customer notification and regulatory timelines:
- Follow legal guidance for notification windows (e.g., GDPR 72-hour notification requirement for certain breaches).
- All customer notifications must be approved by Legal and Product.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Audit readiness checklist:
- Maintain an evidence repository with the following artifacts (examples):
  - Access review attestations (quarterly).
  - IAM policy change logs and approvals.
  - Key rotation logs and KMS audits.
  - Pen test reports and remediation evidence.
  - SDLC pipeline gate logs and SBOMs for releases.
  - Incident reports and postmortem artifacts.

How to collect evidence (process):
1. Identify scope for audit request (systems, time range, tenant).
2. Map required artifacts to owners via the audit checklist.
3. Pull logs from archive (S3 path: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/{audit-id}/raw-logs/).
4. Generate a packaged evidence bundle (PDF + CSV index) and upload to the evidence bucket and Confluence evidence page.
5. Capture approver sign-offs in the evidence index.

Evidence retention & access:
- Evidence bundles for completed audits stored for 7 years.
- Access to evidence bucket is restricted to compliance roles and auditors; access events are logged and audited.

7) Risk Management & Exceptions

Risk acceptance process:
- Any deviation from policy (e.g., extended retention, relaxed RBAC for a service) requires a documented risk exception request.
- Risk request must include: description, justification, compensating controls, impact, proposed expiry date, and monitoring plan.

Approval authority matrix:
- Low-risk exceptions (operational, non-customer-data) - Approver: Engineering manager + Security reviewer.
- High-risk exceptions (customer data, long-term retention, disabling audit features) - Approver: CISO + Legal.

Monitoring & expiry:
- All approved exceptions have a maximum approval period of 90 days unless renewed with explicit justification.
- Owners must provide monthly status updates and evidence of compensating controls.

Exception form template (fields):
- exception_id, owner, requested_by, start_date, expiry_date, risk_summary, compensating_controls, approval_signatures, monitoring_plan

Appendix & runbook snippets

Quick commands and locations:
- Pulling auth events (example):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-log-archive-us-west-2/auth-events/2027/02/ /tmp/auth-events/ --recursive --profile redwood-compliance

- Evidence bundle location pattern: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/{audit-id}/bundle-{timestamp}.zip
